title: Recommendation ITU-R P.684-8: Prediction of field strength at frequencies below about 150 kHz
locators: Scope: field-strength prediction below about 150 kHz
Propagation methods: waveguide and wave-hop; not a bulk-soil conduction or delivered-power model
notes: In-force recommendation as of 2026-11-03. Use as a modern Earth–ionosphere radio-propagation baseline only. It does not validate Tesla's hypothesized bulk-Earth stationary-wave mechanism and does not predict useful load power.

title: Report ITU-R SM.2303-4: Wireless power transmission using technologies other than radio frequency beam
locators: Section 1: non-RF-beam WPT scope and technology overview
EMF safety guidance discussion, pp.27 and following; determination of safety limits is outside ITU-R scope
notes: Technical overview of non-beam WPT and regulatory context. ITU explicitly says EMF safety limits are addressed by other expert organizations; the report points to ICNIRP 2010 at <=100 kHz and ICNIRP 2020 above 100 kHz, alongside IEEE C95.1-2019. Country regulations summarized are not international regulations.

title: ICNIRP Guidelines for Limiting Exposure to Time-Varying Electric and Magnetic Fields (1 Hz to 100 kHz)
authors: International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection
locators: Scope: 1 Hz–100 kHz; selected guidance extends to 10 MHz for nervous-system effects
Exposure basic restrictions and reference levels; not a WPT product performance or instrument measurement standard
notes: Use for the low-frequency exposure regime. At frequencies above 100 kHz additional RF effects and the 2020 RF guidelines must also be considered. National adoption and applicable legal requirements must be checked separately.

title: ICNIRP Guidelines for Limiting Exposure to Electromagnetic Fields (100 kHz to 300 GHz)
authors: International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection
locators: Scope: 100 kHz–300 GHz; basic restrictions and reference levels; dosimetry appendices
notes: Human exposure guideline, not a WPT product performance or measurement standard. Apply with the relevant low-frequency guidance where overlapping effects/frequency ranges require it, and check national adoption.

title: SAE J2954_202408: Wireless Power Transfer for Light-Duty Plug-in/Electric Vehicles and Alignment Methodology
locators: Revised 13 August 2024
Scope: stationary light-duty EV WPT; charging levels up to 11 kVA; surface-mounted installations; forward grid-to-vehicle direction
notes: Not the governing standard for dynamic roadway charging or heavy-duty vehicles. SAE describes heavy-duty and dynamic applications in separate J2954/2 and planned J2954/3 workstreams. This edition specifies unidirectional WPT.

title: IEC 61980-1:2020: Electric vehicle wireless power transfer systems — Part 1: General requirements
locators: Scope: supply-device general requirements for EV WPT
Electrical safety, control communications, efficiency, alignment and EMC; off-board supply equipment scope
notes: Applies to EV WPT supply equipment up to 1,000 V AC and 1,500 V DC. Vehicle-side safety/EMC and maintenance safety are outside the stated scope; motion and bidirectional requirements were under consideration in this edition.

title: IEC 61980-3:2022: Electric vehicle wireless power transfer systems — Part 3: Specific requirements for magnetic field wireless power transfer systems
locators: Scope: off-board magnetic-field WPT supply equipment for stationary electric road vehicles
Sections on characteristics, electrical safety, communications, positioning and EMC
notes: Stationary EV MF-WPT; to be used with IEC 61980-1:2020. Motion, bidirectional, flush-mounted, heavy-duty and >11.1 kVA requirements were listed as under consideration for future documents.

title: IEC PAS 61980-4:2025: Interoperability and safety of high-power wireless power transfer for electric vehicles
locators: Published 25 November 2025
Scope: off-board high-power magnetic-field WPT equipment for stationary electric road vehicles
Safety, basic communications, positioning and EMC requirements
notes: This is a publicly available specification for stationary high-power MF-WPT, not a dynamic-roadway qualification. Do not use it as a blanket safety or performance standard outside its declared scope.

title: IEC/IEEE 63184:2025: Assessment methods of human exposure to electric and magnetic fields from wireless power transfer systems
authors: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
locators: Scope: 3 kHz–30 MHz; SAR, internal electric field, current density and contact current assessment
Assessment procedures; instrumentation and measurement methods; computational methods; combined measurement/computation
notes: Edition 1.0 published 25 February 2025. The IEC scope specifies stationary WPT and focuses on inductive systems. It is an exposure assessment method standard, not a substitute for selecting applicable exposure limits or checking national regulations.

title: P63184: revision project for IEC/IEEE 63184-2025 human-exposure assessment methods for WPT
locators: IEEE Standards Association project page: Active PAR; PAR approval 10 September 2025; explicitly supersedes 63184-2025
Scope displayed by project page: assessment methods for SAR, internal E-fields, current density and contact current; 3 kHz to 30 MHz; focus on inductive WPT
Status is an active revision project, not an approved or published replacement edition as of 3 November 2026
notes: Track as a standards-development project only. IEC/IEEE 63184:2025 remains the published edition; P63184 is an active PAR approved 2025-09-10 and is listed as superseding that edition. Do not cite this PAR as a current normative requirements document or assume capacitive-WPT assessment has already been added. Publisher pages vary in their summary wording: IEEE's standard landing page mentions 1 kHz in its overview, while the title, IEC publication scope and P63184 project page state 3 kHz–30 MHz.

title: Dual-Channel Reconfigurable Topology With Power Class Interoperability for Wireless Charging of EVs
locators: IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, volume 41 issue 10, October 2026, pp.18659-18671; published 30 April 2026; DOI 10.1109/TPEL.2026.3689138

Abstract: six reconfigurable output-power modes across SAE WPT1/WPT2/WPT3 classes; 6.6 kW downscaled prototype; six reported maximum DC-to-DC efficiency values in abstract order: 90.27%, 90.33%, 91.25%, 91.37%, 91.71%, 94.48%

notes: Primary IEEE abstract metadata only. The abstract does not map the six efficiency values to exact power class, mode name, output power, gap, frequency or meter planes. title: A Novel Integrated Wireless Charging System With Reconfigurable Topology for WPT and LVDC
locators: IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, volume 41 issue 11, November 2026, pp.20721-20736; published 17 June 2026; DOI 10.1109/TPEL.2026.3704859
Abstract: 6.8 kW WPT mode at 96.5% efficiency; integrated LVDC mode supplies 1 kW at 89.1% efficiency
Abstract: reuse of receiver-side H-bridge, resonant elements, magnetic core and coils; WPT mode powers HV side with WPT/LV decoupling; LVDC mode provides isolated HV-to-LV conversion
notes: Primary IEEE abstract metadata only. The 1 kW / 89.1% LVDC mode is a distinct wired DC-DC function, not wireless transfer efficiency; it is recorded as an auxiliary engineering metric rather than included in the WPT efficiency lane. Exact WPT efficiency meter planes and conditions require full-text extraction.

title: Modular Series Transmitter Array Based Wireless Charging System for Multiple EV Charging Application
locators: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics, volume 73 issue 2, February 2026, pp.1968-1979; DOI 10.1109/TIE.2025.3605456

Abstract: two-channel laboratory prototype; channels can charge two EVs simultaneously and independently; one EVSE and shared primary LCL compensation; each channel activates/deactivates independently
Abstract: maximum efficiency 95.7% at total output power 4 kW with equal load on both channels; no cross-regulation across load/coupling variation
notes: Primary IEEE abstract metadata only. The abstract does not state exact input/output meter planes, frequency, coil gap, per-channel power split or efficiency uncertainty. The 4 kW figure is total output power across two equal-load channels, not per channel.

title: Magnetic Integration for WPT Systems Using Tightly Coupled Coils With Harmonic Suppressions
locators: IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, volume 41 issue 10, October 2026, pp. 18631-18644; published 28 April 2026; DOI 10.1109/TPEL.2026.3688006
Abstract: 20 kW experimental EV-WPT prototype; measured DC-DC efficiency 90.58%
Abstract: inverter-output current THD reduced from 19.75% to 5.71%; zero-voltage switching maintained over tested operating range
notes: Primary IEEE abstract metadata only. The abstract describes leakage-inductance-based magnetic integration for the primary-side power-conversion module. Exact DC-DC efficiency meter planes, operating conditions, THD measurement location/bandwidth and uncertainty require full-text extraction. Keep the efficiency and THD endpoints as separate metrics; do not infer a whole-vehicle wall-to-battery boundary.

title: Design and implementation of interoperable high-efficiency bidirectional wireless power transfer systems for multiple vehicles
locators: Green Energy and Intelligent Transportation, volume 5 issue 2, April 2026, article 100307; DOI 10.1016/j.geits.2025.100307
Abstract: same grid-side equipment interoperates with three vehicle-side assemblies rated at 6, 11 and 30 kW
Abstract: aligned grid-to-battery efficiency 91.7%-94.3%; aligned battery-to-grid efficiency 89.5%-93.5%
Open full text listed by University of Turku repository; PDF requires extraction for meter planes, mode-to-vehicle mapping, conditions and uncertainty
Full-text Table 1: vehicle-side assembly specifications: 6 kW / 400 V nominal / 380–440 V range / 190–210 mm ground clearance / 85 kHz
Full-text Table 1: vehicle-side assembly specifications: 11 kW / 660 V nominal / 600–700 V range / 160–180 mm ground clearance / 85 kHz
Full-text Table 1: vehicle-side assembly specifications: 30 kW / 550 V nominal / 420–610 V range / 270–290 mm ground clearance / 20 kHz
notes: Peer-reviewed open-access experimental study. The abstract reports ranges across specified operating conditions but does not identify each efficiency endpoint's exact vehicle rating, output power, meter plane, frequency, gap or uncertainty. Do not assign a range endpoint to a vehicle power class without full-text extraction. Rights review remains pending before storing substantial article-derived content. Full-text repository page exposed Table 1 design specifications: 6 kW VA 380–440 V (400 V nominal), 190–210 mm ground clearance, 85 kHz; 11 kW VA 600–700 V (660 V nominal), 160–180 mm, 85 kHz; 30 kW VA 420–610 V (550 V nominal), 270–290 mm, 20 kHz. These are paper-stated target vehicle/VA specifications, not evidence that the published efficiency range endpoints map to each class.

title: A Multiplexing Topology for EV WPT Systems with Integrated PV and Storage
locators: IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, Early Access; published 26 August 2026; DOI 10.1109/TPEL.2026.3727562
Abstract: cascaded H-bridge submodules reuse conversion hardware for PV generation, WPT inversion and storage voltage equalization
Abstract: coordinated control combines maximum-power-point tracking, WPT operation and storage-voltage equalization; experimental validation reported
notes: Architecture-source record only. The accessible abstract gives no quantified efficiency, output power, harmonics, power density, thermal or lifetime results. Do not create numerical prototype measurements until primary-text extraction identifies exact operating modes and meter boundaries.

title: Review on interoperability of wireless charging systems for electric vehicles
locators: Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews, volume 239, October 2026, article 117141; DOI 10.1016/j.rser.2026.117141
Abstract/review scope: coupling structures, load impedance, battery voltage class and output power class interoperability
Review identifies boundary definition, cross-testing and environmental variability as benchmark challenges; recommends standardized benchmark equipment
notes: Secondary review source, not a prototype. Use it to motivate benchmark scope and missing test infrastructure, not as experimental performance evidence. Publisher full text is restricted in the accessible record.
